localFacts.fact: Alhambra (Patronato): photos only without flash and without tripod, monopod or other stabilising element inside the monument – a long monopod does not help there either.
Sagrada Família normativa: no photos or videos with a tripod inside the grounds unless accredited by the press department.
Local terms: visor de ángulo recto / visor angular, pantalla abatible o articulada, columna central, monopié, taburete plegable, rodillera.

localPainPoints.pain: A 1.90 m Spanish photographer says the monopods he tried all make him stoop a lot; forum members ask whether there are monopods for tall people.
localPainPoints.fix: Aim for a monopod of about 178-183 cm (70-72 in) before the head, as the post explains; a 1.86 m owner reaches chin height with a 192 cm monopod.

quotes.text: ¿Y no hay monopiés para gente alta?
Con un bicho que solo se levanta del suelo 1,66m, maese Koldo se nos va a pilllar una lumbalgia del carajo

localPainPoints.pain: Readers confuse the support's height with their own height.
localPainPoints.fix: Compare the support's height with eye/chin height, not head height (body height minus 25-30 cm rule for tripod legs).

quotes.text: piensa que una cosa es la altura del monopie y la otra la de nuestra cima de la cabeza.

localGain.point: Caborian forum thread: 1,66 m monopod for a 1,90 m photographer means back pain ('lumbalgia'), the posture problem of the post in Spanish words.
Alhambra bans tripods AND monopods inside; Sagrada Família bans tripods without accreditation – the flip screen is the only fix that works there.
